Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:25: Further, among the conditions of humility, we learn in the chapter "HaChovel" (Bava Kama, chapter 8, mishnah 7) - these are its words: even though he gives him [compensation], it is not forgiven him until he requests it from him, as it is said (Genesis 20:7), "and now, return the man's wife, for he is a prophet." And from where do we know that if he does not forgive, he is cruel? As it is said (ibid. 20:17), "and Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:26: And they said in the Gemara (92a): our Rabbis taught, all these [payments] mentioned are for the value of the shame, but the payment for anguish - even if he brought all the rams of Nevayot in the world, it is not forgiven him until he requests it from him, as it is said, "return the man's wife," and so on - to this point, relevant here. And Rashi, peace be upon him, explained: "all these mentioned" - a sela, a maneh, two hundred, four hundred [zuz] as the value of the shame - but the anguish over which he worries because of his own shame is not forgiven him [merely by payment] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:27: And in the Tosefta of "HaChovel" (9:11) it is taught: one who injures his fellow, even if the injurer did not ask [forgiveness] of the injured party, the injured party must seek mercy for him, as it is said (Genesis 20:17), "and Abraham prayed to God." And so you find with Job's companions, as it is said (Job 42:8), "take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams" - what is written after it? (ibid. 42:10), "and the LORD restored Job's fortunes." Rabbi Yehudah in the name of Rabban Gamliel: behold it says (Deuteronomy 13:18), "and He shall give you mercy, and have mercy on you, and multiply you" - let this sign be in your hand: as long as you are merciful, the Merciful One shall have mercy on you - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:28: Further, they said in the Midrash (Yalkut, Psalms, mizmor 10, siman 648, page 93a): Rabbi Yissachar of Kfar Mando said, and if Joseph, who forgave his brothers, as it is written (Genesis 45:8), "it was not you who sent me here" - see how great this is - one who does not forgive, all the more so [is culpable] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:29: Further, they said in the Midrash (Yalkut Shmuel, siman 151, page 23b), concerning Shimi, when he came to David to ask his forgiveness, he said (II Samuel 19:21), "and behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph" - these are its words: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani came up from Babylon. Rabbi Yonatan asked him, what is the meaning of "and behold, I have come today, the first of all the house of Joseph"? He said to him, when Shimi came to David, he said to him, just as Joseph's brothers repaid him evil and he repaid them good, so I have repaid you evil - repay me with good - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:30: Further, among the conditions of submission, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 4): when he encounters the wise, who know God and His Torah, who are close to God, [he should submit before them], as it is said (Psalms 141:5), "let the righteous strike me in kindness, and rebuke me," and it says (Proverbs 14:19), "the evil bow before the good" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:31: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in the chapter "Arvei Pesachim" (113b): from where do we know that if one knows his fellow to be greater than him even in one matter, he is obligated to treat him with honor? Scripture says (Daniel 6:4), "because an extraordinary spirit was in him" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:32: And in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 166a-b), on the verse (Job 32:2), "Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram" - it says, Elihu was a priest, and from the seed of Ezekiel the prophet, was he - it is written here, "son of Barachel the Buzite," and it is written there, "Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest." And it said further, why was he called "the Buzite"? Because he disgraced [mevazeh] himself before whoever was greater than him, and therefore he ascended to the supernal name, "Buzi" - this one is called a complete man in everything, unlike "ben adam" [son of man] used here [of Ezekiel, a lower designation], as it is written (Ezekiel 2:6), "and you, son of man" - and because he ascended to this name, he is called "Ram" [exalted], supernal above all - and therefore he said (Job 32:6), "I am young in days [tze'ir ani leyamim], and you are aged" - it should say "of days" [miyamim]; what is "leyamim"? Rather, he said, I am young, and I make myself small, "to the days" [leyamim] compared to a person who has many days - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:33: And of this category is what is said in the Mishnah, chapter 5 of Avot (mishnah 7): seven characteristics in a boor, and seven in a sage - a sage does not speak before one greater than him in wisdom - and the rest of the attributes stated in the mishnah contain some of the ways of humility, such as concerning what he has not heard, he says, I have not heard, and likewise he does not interrupt his fellow's words, and is not hasty to answer - for this requires the subduing of the inclination.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:34: Further, among the conditions of humility, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 4): when they praise him for his good attributes, he must submit and pass over in his mind the sins and transgressions that preceded, which the Creator knew and covered over and was patient with, so that he return from them - and he should not rejoice in people's mistaken opinion of him, but rather mourn, since the Creator, blessed be He, truly knows the evil of his deeds, and His refraining from repaying him and rewarding him according to his own goodness - and he shall submit in his heart, as it is said (Psalms 38:19), "for I shall declare my iniquity."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:35: Further, he wrote elsewhere (Gate of Submission, chapter 7) that if they praise him for a good deed, he should disdain the one who praises him for it, and it shall be lowly and small in his own soul, from being accepted and pleasing before the Creator, because of its smallness compared to what he is obligated in from the multiples of that good deed - and he should say to the one praising him, my brother, this is not against my sins, but like a spark of fire in the sea, and even if it were considered something, how do we know whether it is saved from the harms of loss that overtake it, until the Creator accept it from me and not turn it back upon me and cast it in my face, as it is written (Isaiah 1:12), "when you come to appear before Me," and so on. All the more so if they praise him falsely, he must distance that matter from himself, and say to the one telling it, it is enough for me, my brother, in brief, what I am obligated in to the Creator - do not add to me the sin of falling short and the sin of the praise for what I have not done, for I know my own sins and transgressions, as David said (Psalms 51:5), "for I know my transgressions."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:36: And so the sign of humility is that when God does him good with great goodness, exceeding wisdom, abundant understanding, or great wealth, or also honor before royalty and the like - things people are accustomed to boast of and be proud of - he remains in the state of lowliness he had before this. The explanation of his words: he remains in the lowliness he had before he had the greatness and wisdom - and he has added nothing but humility and lowliness before God, and honor and goodness for people - as Abraham said, at the time the Creator praised him, saying (Genesis 18:17), "shall I hide from Abraham," and he said, "and I am dust and ashes" (ibid. 18:27); and Moses said (Exodus 16:7), "and what are we?"; and King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 22:7), "and I am a worm, and not a man" - then you shall understand his inward state and know his submission - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:37: And in Midrash Mishlei it says, on the verse (Proverbs 27:2), "let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth; a foreigner, and not your own lips."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:38: And in the Zohar (Parashat Terumah, page 129a) they said that at the time Israel finish the holiness of the [Torah] portion, then a herald goes out and says, supernal and lower beings, pay heed: who is haughty of spirit concerning the words of Torah? Who is one whose every word is meant to exalt himself with words of Torah? For we have learned, a person must be lowly in this world regarding words of Torah, for there is no height in Torah except in the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:39: And in the Zohar (Parashat Shelach Lecha, page 158a) they said that Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa were walking on the road, and encountered a certain man, and asked him, who are you? He said, I am a Jew. And they asked him whether he occupied himself with Torah, and he said, behold, I occupy myself with Torah through the merit of a certain son of mine, whom I brought into the study house, and through him I profit in Torah. Rabbi Chizkiyah said, through your son's merit it is good, but the matter we are engaged in - we see that it needs to be elevated to another place. That man said, tell your own matter, for sometimes in the sackcloth of a poor man a pearl is found. After he expounded for them the verse they asked him about, they said to him, would you like to walk with us? He said to them, if I do this, Torah shall call me a fool, and moreover I would be liable with my own soul. They said to him, why? He said to them, for I am a messenger, and King Solomon said (Proverbs 26:6), "he who sends a message by the hand of a fool cuts off his own feet and drinks violence." After he left, Rabbi Chizkiyah and Rabbi Yesa encountered some people and asked about that man, who is he? They told them, he is Rabbi Chagai, a colleague among the colleagues, and so on. Rabbi Yesa said, certainly this is Rabbi Chagai, for all his days he never wished to show himself in what he knew - and therefore he told us that his son merited him in Torah, since Scripture says (Proverbs 26:12), "do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him" - certainly he is a trustworthy messenger - to this point. And from this teaching you shall see the merit of the early ones, that even in a place where they were not known, they would not make themselves known.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:40: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said in Aggadat Shmuel (chapter 14) that because Samuel said (I Samuel 9:19), "I am the seer," he was punished - these are its words: "I am the seer" - Rabbi Yehoshua of Sichnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi, the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, Samuel, you call yourself a seer - I shall show you a thing you shall not see. When did He tell him this? At the time He told him (I Samuel 16:1), "fill your horn with oil," and so on, "and the LORD said, do not look at his appearance," and so on. And similarly, "and the matter that is too hard for you" (Deuteronomy 1:17), as we copied in chapter 2.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:41: And so David was punished because he said (Psalms 119:54), "Your statutes have been my songs" - these are its words (Sotah 35a): Rava expounded, why was David punished through Uzza, as it is written (II Samuel 6:7), "and God struck him there for [his] error"? Because he called the Torah scroll "songs," saying, "Your statutes have been my songs" - the Holy One, blessed be He, said to him, words of Torah, of which it is written (Proverbs 23:5), "will you cast your eyes upon it, and it is gone" - you call them songs? Behold, I shall cause you to stumble over a matter that even schoolchildren know, as it is written (Numbers 7:9), "but to the sons of Kehat he gave none, because the service of the holy things was upon them," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:42: And one who praises himself for his wisdom is a fool, as we say (Bava Metzia 85b): Rav Chama said, what is the meaning of (Proverbs 14:33), "wisdom rests in the heart of one who understands"? This is a Torah scholar, son of a Torah scholar. "But in the midst of fools it becomes known" - this is a Torah scholar, son of an ignoramus [who must proclaim his own wisdom]. Ulla said, this is what people say, a coin in an empty jug rattles loudly - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:43: And in the Zohar (Parashat Balak, page 193b), concerning Balaam, who praised himself and said (Numbers 23:15), "and I shall meet [God] thus" - and they raised a difficulty there: behold it is said, "and there did not arise a prophet again in Israel like Moses," but among the nations of the world one did arise - but if all this were truly in his hand, and he was so powerful in wisdom that he praised himself with such powerful might, saying, "and I shall meet thus, I shall uproot from this" - how could they [the Israelites] kill him [i.e., how could such a powerful figure be defeated]? Rather, in the book of wisdom of King Solomon it is thus said: there are three signs - a sign of a transgression is jaundice; a sign of foolishness is much talk; a sign that one knows nothing is self-praise. And this determines the rest: a fool in all transgressions, everything is in him. And behold it is written, "let a stranger praise you and not your own mouth" - and if not a stranger, then your own mouth [i.e., there is no other option but to boast falsely]. Not so - rather, if there is no one who recognizes you, open your mouth to speak and make known true words of Torah, and then, through the opening of your mouth, they shall praise and know who you are - for there is nothing in the world by which people recognize a person except at the time he opens his mouth; his mouth shall make known to people who he is. That wicked Balaam, self-praiser, praised himself in everything, and yet with all this he stole minds and exalted himself with his own words - to this point. And there it explained that he praised himself, "the utterance of one who hears the sayings of God and knows the knowledge of the Most High" (Numbers 24:16) - for whoever hears these words would think he was a great prophet, though it was not so, as explained there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:44: And similar to this they explained in the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah 16:3) - these are its words: Rabbi Yehoshua of Sichnin said in the name of Rabbi Levi, they said to the Euphrates, why does your voice not travel? It said to them, I have no need - my deeds make me known: a person plants a sapling by me, and it grows in thirty days; he sows a vegetable by me, and it stands ready in three days. They said to the Tigris, why does your voice travel? It said to them, would that we could make our own voice heard and be seen [i.e., it lacks the same visible produce]. They said to the fruit trees, why does your voice not travel? They said to them, we have no need - our fruits testify for us. They said to the barren trees, why does your voice travel? They said to them, would that we could make our own voice heard and be seen - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:45: And nevertheless, it is permitted for a person to make himself known in a place where he is not known, as we say in Nedarim (62a): Rava raised a contradiction - it is written (I Kings 18:12), "and your servant has feared the LORD from his youth," and it is written (Proverbs 27:2), "let a stranger praise you, and not your own mouth" - this is not difficult: this [verse of Elijah] is in a place where he is known, and that [verse of Proverbs] is in a place where he is not known - for Rava said, it is permitted for a person to make himself known in a place where he is not known - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:46: And so they said in Midrash Mishlei (26:4-5): "do not answer a fool according to his folly" - and what is written after it? "Answer a fool according to his folly" - Rav Huna said, "do not answer a fool" in a place where he is known and you are known, lest you too become like him, so that they not say, come and see a wise man doing business with a fool. Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, "answer a fool according to his folly" in a place where neither you nor he are known - why? Lest he be wise in his own eyes, so that they not say, had he not been suspect in the matters he speaks of, this one would not have been silent to him [i.e., his silence would seem to concede the fool's point]. And so it says (Proverbs 26:8), "like binding a stone in a sling, so is giving honor to a fool" - Rabbi Alexandri said, whoever gives honor to a fool is like one who casts a stone at Mercurius [an idol] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:47: Further, among the customs of submission, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 4) - these are its words: and the seventh, when he occupies himself with a deed of service, such as charity, prayer, and a mitzvah, he should not occupy himself with it while placing pride and haughtiness in his heart, but rather submit and be lowly before the Creator, in what is revealed of him and what is hidden, and not consider it as anything in his own soul, compared to the greatness of what he owes to God from the multiples of that deed, as it is written (Micah 6:6-7), "with what shall I approach the LORD," and so on, "will the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:48: And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained in Tractate Berachot (10b) a matter similar to this - these are their own words: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Yosei ben Zimra, whoever relies on his own merit is given [an outcome that depends on] the merit of others, and whoever relies on the merit of others is given [an outcome depending on] his own merit. Moses relied on the merit of others, as it is said (Exodus 32:13), "remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants" - therefore they relied for him on his own merit, as it is said (Psalms 106:23), "and He said He would destroy them, had not Moses, His chosen one," and so on. Chizkiyahu relied on his own merit, as it is said (II Kings 20:3), "remember now how I have walked before You" - therefore they relied for him on the merit of others, as it is said (ibid. 19:34), "and I will defend this city, for My sake and for the sake of My servant David" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:49: Further, in Sanhedrin (93b), that Nehemiah was punished because he said (Nehemiah 5:19), "remember me, my God, for good" - these are its words: consider, Ezra said all the matters of Nehemiah [i.e. authored much of the shared narrative] - but why is Nehemiah ben Chachalyah's book not called by his own name? Rabbi Yirmiyah bar Abba said, because he claimed credit for his own good deeds, saying, "remember me, my God, for good." David too said (Psalms 106:4), "remember me, LORD, with the favor of Your people" - he did not say it that way [i.e. he attributed it to communal favor, not personal claim] - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:50: And the pious Rabbi Yosef Yavetz, peace be upon him, wrote, on the mishnah (Avot, chapter 2, mishnah 13), "do not make your prayer a fixed routine, but rather mercy and supplications before the Omnipresent" - for this is the distinction between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva: Rabbi Eliezer recited twenty-four blessings [of supplication] and was not answered, while Rabbi Akiva said "Avinu Malkeinu" and was answered (Ta'anit 25b) - for Rabbi Eliezer had the merit of the ancestors and trusted in his own merit and theirs, while Rabbi Akiva had no ancestral merit, being the son of converts, and did not consider himself anything - therefore he was answered.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:51: And so a person must ask only from the supernal storehouse, which is the storehouse of free gifts, as Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, asked, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Devarim Rabbah 2:1) on "and I pleaded with the LORD" (Deuteronomy 3:23).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:52: Further, among the customs of the submissive one, the author of Chovot HaLevavot wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 4), that when the Creator does him good in this world with wealth and abundant money, he should submit to God because of the heaviness of the burden of the obligation of thanksgiving for it, and be lowly before Him out of fear that it not become a punishment, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:12), "wealth is kept by its owner to his own harm."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:53: And so they expounded in the Midrash HaNe'elam (Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 121b) - these are its words: and all those who were marked by the image of Adam the first man, through it they were struck and died - for such is the way of the Holy One, blessed be He: He gives wealth to a person - why? To feed the poor and perform His commandments. If he does not do this, and becomes proud through it, that very wealth is what strikes him, as it is written, "wealth is kept by its owner to his own harm." He gives him children - why? To teach them the ways of the Holy One, blessed be He, and to keep His commandments, as it is said of Abraham (Genesis 18:19), "for I have known him, so that he shall command his children and his household after him, and they shall keep the way of the LORD, to do righteousness and justice," and so on - if he does not do this, and becomes proud through them, he is struck, as it is written (Job 18:19), "he has no offspring or descendant among his people." And likewise, when the Holy One, blessed be He, gives from the good, supernal beauty of Adam the first man to them - why? In order to keep His commandments and do His will - if they do not do so, and become proud through it, they are struck through this very beauty - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:54: And further, when he reads in the Torah and in the books of the Prophets and sees the reward and the punishment, and knows in his own soul that he has fallen short of his duty to God, he is obligated to submit and be lowly before the Creator, blessed be He, out of fear of Him and His punishment, as it is said of Josiah (II Kings 22:11), "and it came to pass, when the king heard the words of the LORD, that he tore his garments" - and the Creator said to him (ibid. 22:19), "because your heart was tender, and you submitted before Me," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:55: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 6), that he should be precious of spirit and exalted of soul concerning matters of the World to Come, that he not be satisfied with whatever comes his way of them, and should not say, enough with whatever comes to hand of them - but rather, his own deeds, ability, and effort should seem small in his own eyes, and his soul should always be exalted toward what is above this, as it is said of Jehoshaphat (II Chronicles 17:6), "and his heart was exalted in the ways of the LORD" - and he should complain against himself for his own falling short in matters of Torah, before God and before people, and seek help and strength from God - and he should set aside for the honor of the Creator, and abandon greatness and preciousness at the time he serves God, blessed be He, whether alone or in the midst of assemblies of people - as it was said of Aaron, concerning the greatness of his own level, "and he shall remove the ashes," and so on (Leviticus 6:3), and the Creator obligated him to take this out every single day, continuously, in order to lower him and remove haughtiness from his heart - and so they said of David (II Samuel 6:16), "and she saw King David leaping and dancing before the LORD," and he said (Psalms 119:46), "and I shall speak of Your testimonies before kings, and shall not be ashamed."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:56: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, chapter 6), that he should rise up against the wicked for the honor of the Creator, and his own forgiveness toward people should not lead him astray, in disciplining himself, to forgive on a matter of God, or on behalf of one who spoke against His prophets, His pious ones, and His treasured people - and he should not conduct himself, regarding the oppression of one person by another, according to his own custom of forgiving them when they oppress him personally, but rather he should save the oppressed and help rescue him from the hand of the oppressor, as it is written (Jeremiah 21:12), "execute justice in the morning, and deliver the robbed from the hand of the oppressor" - and Job said (Job 29:17), "and I broke the fangs of the unjust," and so on - and he should instruct people in the service of God, and rebuke them and shame them, and command them concerning the good and warn them of evil, both by his hand and by his tongue, as it is said of Pinchas (Psalms 106:30), "then Pinchas stood up and executed judgment, and it was accounted to him as righteousness for generation after generation, forever."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:57: And in the Zohar (Parashat Vayechi, page 239a) it explained the verse (Psalms 37:1), "do not compete with evildoers" - these are its words: what is "al titchar" [do not compete]? It should say "al titchaber" [do not associate] - rather, "do not compete" [make a display of rivalry] with evildoers, because you do not know your own root and cannot bear it - perhaps it is a tree that shall never be uprooted, and you shall be pushed away before it. "Do not envy those who do iniquity" - do not pay heed to their deeds and do not come to envy them, for whoever sees their deeds and does not become jealous for the sake of the Holy One, blessed be He, transgresses three prohibitions, as it is written (Exodus 20:3-5), "you shall have no other gods before Me; you shall not make yourself a carved image or any likeness; you shall not bow to them nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God" - therefore a person must separate himself from them and turn his way away from them - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:58: Further, he wrote (Gate of Submission, there), that he should content himself, for the causes of sustenance, with whatever happens to come and whatever he finds, so that his soul become disgraced and lowly in his own eyes, and to train it to withstand its own bodily desire, and to turn to repay the goodness of the Creator for the greatness of His goodness and the abundance of His kindness toward him, as King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 119:32), "I shall run the way of Your commandments." And he should have few words, a lowered voice, little laughter, and little swearing by the Name even for the truth, and no lie should pass over his tongue, and he should not sit in the company of jesters, and should not rejoice in what the ignorant masses rejoice in, from the pleasures of the world, out of submission and lowliness, not from the side of greatness and self-exaltation - as the prophet said (Jeremiah 15:17), "I did not sit in the company of jesters, nor did I rejoice; because of Your hand I sat alone, for You have filled me with indignation" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:59: And when a person remembers the matter of the exile of the Shechinah, which, because of our sins, is in exile, as it says (Isaiah 50:1), "and for your transgressions your mother was sent away," and "like a bird wandering from its nest, so is a man who wanders from his place" (Proverbs 27:8) - this refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, of whom it is written (Exodus 15:3), "the LORD is a man of war," as explained in the Tikkunim (page 1b) - and our sins have prolonged our end - it is fitting that he submit truly and not let joy enter his heart over all the blemish he has caused through his sins.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:60: And they said in the Tikkunim (page 108b), concerning the exile of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, that in exile the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah clothe themselves in the ten lower crowns [of impurity] - these are its words: and these husks are a partition between Israel and their Father in Heaven - in these husks the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah clothe themselves, to fulfill, of His Shechinah, (Psalms 103:19), "and His kingdom rules over everything," and to fulfill of Him (ibid. 47:8), "for God is King of all the earth." But above, in His own place, it is said (ibid. 5:5), "evil shall not sojourn with You" - rather, His own husks above are garments of several beautiful colors of light, from which the Holy One, blessed be He, as it were spreads Himself in exile and clothes Himself in these others, in order to guard Israel, who clothe themselves in these husks - and this is (Isaiah 63:9), "in all their affliction, He was afflicted."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:61: And it said afterward that these husks cause separation between the Holy One, blessed be He, and Israel, and this is the secret of (ibid. 59:2), "but your iniquities have separated between you and your God."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:62: And it said further afterward: and the ten holy garments, of them it is said, "the LORD dwells alone, outside the camp is his dwelling" [play on leprosy laws] - in that husk which a person has caused the Name of the LORD to be clothed in, He takes vengeance from him for it - and therefore (Exodus 20:7), "you shall not take the Name of the LORD your God in vain" - and therefore they established, in Havdalah, "who separates between holy and profane, and between light and darkness," so that the husks of the profane not attach - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:63: And behold, it is explicit that our sins cause the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to be clothed in ten husks, and of this it is said, "but your iniquities have separated," and likewise, "He dwells alone" - and that very husk that our sins caused the Holy One, blessed be He, to be clothed in there shall take retribution from us for it, as explained in the teaching. If so, how could he rejoice, knowing how much he has sinned and how many partition upon partition he has caused the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah to be clothed in - and this is the cause of the prolongation of the exile.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Humility 6:64: And further, in Midrash Eichah (Introduction, 10): "you have enslaved Me with your sins" (Isaiah 43:24) - see what your sins have caused: to destroy My House, burn My Sanctuary, exile My children among the nations of the world, and leave Me sitting alone - "how [Eicha] does she sit alone" - to this point. And of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 97b, Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 42), that Israel are redeemed only through repentance, so that the husks be broken.
